title: Two forms of unbounded prime gaps
content: Answers the open question `infinitude-primes-oq-02` (how large can gaps between consecutive primes grow?) with: without bound. Two complementary elementary statements are proved via the factorial construction — a block of $G$ consecutive composites $(G+1)!+2,\dots,(G+1)!+(G+1)$, and two consecutive primes $p<q$ with $q-p\ge G$. This is the *large*-gap counterpart to the gallery's *small*-gap `bounded-prime-gaps` work, and it discharges the `large_prime_gaps_exist` axiom.
mathContext: For all $G$: $\exists$ $G$ consecutive composites, and $\exists$ consecutive primes $p<q$ with $q-p\ge G$.

title: not_prime_factorial_add: the one workhorse lemma
content: For $2\le j\le G+1$, $(G+1)!+j$ is not prime. The proof uses `Nat.not_prime_iff_exists_dvd_ne` and exhibits $j$ itself as the nontrivial divisor: $j\mid(G+1)!$ (via `Nat.dvd_factorial` since $0<j\le G+1$) and $j\mid j$, so $j\mid(G+1)!+j$; the strict bounds $1<j<(G+1)!+j$ (closed by `omega` using `factorial_pos`) make the divisor proper. Every later result is an application of this single fact.

title: exists_consecutive_composites: arbitrarily long runs
content: For every $G$, exhibits $m=(G+1)!+2$ with $m,\dots,m+(G-1)$ all composite. The proof reindexes $m+i=(G+1)!+(i+2)$ (so $2\le i+2\le G+1$ when $i<G$) and applies `not_prime_factorial_add` to each term. This is the 'gap' in raw form: $G$ consecutive integers with no prime among them.

title: exists_large_prime_gap: prime-free block and the prime above
content: The consecutive-prime statement. Sets $M=(G+1)!$ and shows the block $[M+2,M+G+1]$ is prime-free (`hrun`, again from `not_prime_factorial_add`). Takes $q$ = the least prime $\ge M+2$ using `Nat.find` on `Nat.exists_infinite_primes`, which yields both $q$ and its minimality certificate `hq_min`. Since every element of the block is composite, minimality forces $q\ge M+G+2$ (`hq_big`, by `by_contra`).

title: The prime below and the consecutive-prime assembly
content: Takes $p$ = the greatest prime $\le M+1$ via `Nat.findGreatest`, nonzero because 2 is prime and $2\le M+1$ (`Nat.le_findGreatest`), with `Nat.findGreatest_is_greatest` certifying maximality. Assembles the final tuple: $p<q$ and $p+G\le q$ (both by `omega` from $p\le M+1$, $q\ge M+G+2$), plus no prime strictly between — a candidate $k$ is case-split at $M+1$ and refuted by `hp_greatest` (below) or `hq_min` (above).
mathContext: $p=\max\{x\le M+1:\ x\text{ prime}\}$; $p,q$ consecutive with $q-p\ge G$.

title: Worked demonstrations
content: Two `example`s instantiate the general theorems at concrete parameters: 100 consecutive composite numbers (from `exists_consecutive_composites 100`) and a pair of consecutive primes differing by at least 1000 (from `exists_large_prime_gap 1000`). They serve as machine-checked sanity checks that the universally quantified results specialise correctly.
